draft.title: Australia's health system and equity
card: Medicare
Australia's public health insurance. It pays all or part of the cost of many doctor visits, tests and public hospital care.
PBS
The Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme lowers the price of many prescription medicines.
Private insurance
People pay to cover costs such as private hospital care and some extras. The government encourages it, but it is a choice.
Equity means fair access to care based on need. The NDIS also funds disability support. These schemes aim for equity, but gaps remain, such as out-of-pocket costs and fewer services in remote areas.
draft.remember: Australia's schemes aim to share access to care fairly, but some people still miss out.

a.q: Which scheme lowers the price of many prescription medicines?
opts: The PBS
Medicare
Private health insurance
The NDIS
a.why: The PBS is the scheme that subsidises prescription medicines. Medicare is the tempting answer, but it covers things like doctor visits, tests and public hospital care.
a.clue: Look for the scheme with medicines in its name.

b.q: Jess lives in a remote town and must travel hours to see a specialist, even though she has Medicare. What does this show?
opts: A gap in equity remains despite the schemes
Medicare does not cover specialist care at all
Private insurance is compulsory for rural people
The PBS has failed to lower medicine prices
b.why: Having Medicare does not guarantee easy access, as distance and fewer services in remote areas can leave gaps. Medicare does help pay for many services, so saying it covers none is wrong.
b.clue: Having a card is not the same as being able to get care.

b.best: A gap in equity remains despite the schemes

proposal.title: Australia's health system and equity
card: Medicare
Australia's public health insurance. It pays all or part of the cost of many GP visits, specialist visits with a referral, tests and public hospital care.
PBS
The Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme lowers the price people pay at the chemist for many prescription medicines.
Private insurance
People pay to cover costs such as private hospital care and some extras, like dental. The government encourages it, but it is a choice.
Equity means fair access to care based on need. The NDIS also funds disability support. These schemes aim for equity, but gaps remain, such as out-of-pocket costs and fewer services in remote areas.
proposal.remember: Australia's schemes aim to share access to care fairly, but some people still miss out.

a.q: Ravi's GP prescribes a medicine, and he pays far less than its full price at the chemist. Which scheme explains this?
opts: The PBS
Medicare
Private health insurance
The NDIS
a.why: The PBS lowers the price of many prescription medicines bought at the chemist. Medicare is the tempting answer, but it pays towards things like doctor visits, tests and public hospital care, not the medicine itself.
a.clue: Think about where Ravi saved money: the clinic or the chemist.

b.q: Jess lives in a remote town and must travel hours to see a specialist, even though she has Medicare. What does this show?
opts: A gap in equity remains despite the schemes
Medicare does not cover specialist care at all
Private insurance is compulsory for rural people
The PBS has failed to lower medicine prices
b.why: Having Medicare does not guarantee easy access, as distance and fewer services in remote areas can leave gaps. Medicare does pay towards specialist visits when a person has a referral, so the problem is getting to the care, not a lack of cover.
b.clue: Having a card is not the same as being able to get care.
